name: American Samoa
prevalence_note: No territorial scam bulletin was found; USPS serves American Samoa, and the US Postal Inspection Service warns about fake tracking texts and fake USPS calls that apply here too.
cross_border_note: American Samoa (+1-684) sits in the NANP, so +1 spoofed numbers from the mainland look domestic; long mainland parcel transit times make delivery-problem texts more believable.

scams.name: Fake USPS tracking text
scams.name_en: Fake USPS delivery-problem text with a link, applied to American Samoa
scams.signals_en: A text claims a USPS parcel cannot be delivered and sends the owner to a link to update an address or pay a small fee.
scams.legit_en: USPIS says USPS does not text tracking links unless the customer signed up with a tracking number.
bait_tactics: Ask which mainland sender shipped it and the tracking number, then compare it slowly
Say the parcel will be asked about at the Pago Pago post office counter

scams.name: Fake USPS phone call
scams.name_en: Caller posing as USPS asking for personal data, applied to American Samoa
scams.signals_en: Someone claiming to be USPS phones about a held package and asks for identity or card details to release it.
scams.legit_en: USPIS warns USPS does not phone customers asking for personal information or payment.
bait_tactics: Ask for the caller's post office branch and supervisor's name
Say mail questions only go to the local post office in person
